headline: Your HexaGroup waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing energy and industrial firms into the right Growth Engine offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Alberto Bernardoni. A Clay workflow is ready to stand up with this spec.
productSummary: HexaGroup helps energy and industrial firms hatch bold ideas and scale them with precision. Growth Engines bridge branding, marketing, sales, and service so CX runs in lockstep. Work arrives as a custom Growth Engine, a rapidly tailored GOpack, or a project-based engagement. HexaGroup is a member-owner of BBN and does not replace the client's team. It extends it.
coreInsight: Charlotte already opened on energy and industrial firms, writing to CMOs and Business Development Managers. The one TAM stays there. The one routing ladder is public growth pressure: marketing leadership hiring first, then sales and BD hiring, then a named project launch, then every remaining energy or industrial firm.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is public growth pressure
sections.takeaway: Open marketing or BD seats, then a named project launch, tell you which HexaGroup motion the firm needs now. LinkedIn Jobs and the newsroom carry that without a paid data product.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes the energy and industrial TAM
sections.takeaway: First match wins. CMO and marketing leadership hiring, then BD and sales hiring, then a recent launch, then the GOsurvey catch-all.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each pressure gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Marketing hires get a silo / brand sketch. BD hires get sales lockstep. Launch accounts get a CX brief on the named project. Everyone else gets a GOsurvey.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Charlotte's three angles, mapped onto the waterfall
sections.takeaway: The list is always energy and industrial, aimed at CMOs and BDMs. Project-launch personalization is a tier, not a side quest. Brand-integration versus sales-growth is the A/B on those same routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the hire or the launch
sections.takeaway: Notice the req or the project, poke the silo between brand, marketing, sales, and service, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the CMO-hire tier, then stand up Clay
sections.takeaway: Start where the mandate is on the job board. Load the same routing spec into the Clay workflow Charlotte already offered.

signalReasons: LinkedIn Jobs and careers pages show CMO, marketing, BD, and sales seats without buying a vertical database.
Company newsrooms and Google News name plant, terminal, product, and market-entry launches, which is the CX pain Charlotte wanted personalized.
The ladder maps to live HexaGroup copy: Growth Engines exist because branding, marketing, sales, and service sitting in silos clips growth.
Every remaining energy or industrial firm still gets a GOsurvey route, so coverage is 100% of TAM.

routingRules.if: remaining energy or industrial firm in TAM

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: CMO / marketing hire
tiers.trigger: Open CMO, VP Marketing, Head of Marketing, Head of Growth, or Brand Director seat
tiers.pain: The firm just approved a marketing leadership seat, which usually means brand, demand, and CX are still sitting in separate owners. A new hire without a system becomes another silo.
tiers.valueProp: HexaGroup plugs in as a high-performance layer on top of brand and GTM. Growth Engines integrate branding, marketing, sales, and service without adding a parallel headcount. They do not replace the team. They extend it.
tiers.replyDensity: Highest intent. Budget and mandate are already on the req.

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: BD / sales hire
tiers.trigger: Open BDM, VP Sales, Director of Business Development, or CRO seat, and no marketing-leadership req
tiers.pain: Sales is being asked to grow while marketing and service still hand off a different story. Pipeline gets sluggish and credibility with customers drops, which is the silo problem HexaGroup writes on the Growth Engine page.
tiers.valueProp: Growth Engines put marketing and sales in sync, shorten the messy handoff, and keep service feeding the next conversation. Entry can be a GOpack if they need lift faster than a custom build.
tiers.replyDensity: Strong. The seat is a growth number, not a brand workshop.

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Named project launch
tiers.trigger: A plant, terminal, product line, or new-market launch in the last 90 days, and no growth hire already routed
tiers.pain: The firm launched something real, then brand, sales, and service did not move in lockstep around it. Buyers feel the CX gap on day one of the new offer.
tiers.valueProp: HexaGroup's project-based path is built for this: introducing a solution into a new market, repositioning for the energy transition, or standing up the site and story around a milestone. GridPoint is the named CX-integration proof on their site (10x brand valuation).
tiers.replyDensity: Good when the project name is in the first line.

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: GOsurvey / engineered growth
tiers.trigger: Every remaining energy or industrial firm in the TAM
tiers.pain: Growth is still ad hoc. Branding, marketing, sales, and service run in parallel, so the firm keeps buying projects instead of a system.
tiers.valueProp: The GO process is the low-friction door: pick custom, GOpack, or project-based, outline budget, complete the GOsurvey, and HexaGroup sends a Growth Engine proposal within 10 business days.
tiers.dataSource: Energy and industrial TAM pull after higher tiers route out
tiers.replyDensity: Broadest coverage. Softest ask. Still 100% of TAM.

campaigns.name: Silo / Growth Engine Sketch
campaigns.filter: Open CMO / VP / Head of Marketing / Head of Growth / Brand Director
campaigns.strategy: Name the open role and the silo the hire will inherit, then offer a Growth Engine sketch
campaigns.overview: Charlotte angle 1 + 3. Scrape energy and industrial firms, write to the CMO track, and lead with brand, marketing, sales, and service in lockstep.

campaigns.name: Sales-growth variant on the CMO hire
campaigns.filter: Same Tier 1 list, sales-growth copy instead of brand copy
campaigns.strategy: Keep the req as the notice line. Swap the poke to pipeline and valuation instead of brand strength.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the silo sketch. Same exclusive route, sales-growth language.

campaigns.name: Sales Lockstep Teardown
campaigns.filter: Open BDM / VP Sales / Director BD / CRO, no marketing-leadership req
campaigns.strategy: Name the sales seat and the marketing/service handoff, then offer lockstep
campaigns.overview: Charlotte's BDM target as its own tier, not a mixed CMO list.

campaigns.name: Brand-integration variant on the BD hire
campaigns.filter: Same Tier 2 list, brand copy instead of sales copy
campaigns.strategy: Keep the BD seat in the first line. Lead with brand as a revenue-generating asset rather than more pipeline activity.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the lockstep teardown. Same waterfall, brand-integration language.

campaigns.name: Launch CX Brief
campaigns.filter: Named project / plant / product / market entry in the last 90 days
campaigns.overview: Charlotte angle 2. Recent project launches and CX pain are the route, not a P.S. on a generic email.

campaigns.name: GOsurvey snapshot
campaigns.strategy: Industry-segment notice line, GOsurvey as the tiny yes
campaigns.overview: Catch-all so the scrape of energy and industrial firms still covers 100% of TAM.

campaigns.name: Brand versus sales catch-all A/B
campaigns.filter: Same catch-all list, split brand-integration vs sales-growth first line
campaigns.strategy: Do not change routing. Split only the value prop sentence.
campaigns.overview: Charlotte angle 3 on the remainder, after higher-intent tiers have a control.

launchPlan: Build the energy and industrial TAM in LinkedIn Sales Nav, then pull open marketing-leadership and BD/sales reqs before any enrichment.
Stand up the Clay workflow Charlotte already offered, with the same exclusive routing spec and merge fields.
Launch Tier 1 CMO / marketing-hire first. Brand-integration copy as the control, sales-growth as the A/B on the same list.
Add Tier 2 BD / sales-hire, then Tier 3 named launches once the newsroom scrape is wiring clean project names.
Turn on the GOsurvey catch-all last so every remaining energy or industrial account still has a route.

thresholds.rate: Dense positive replies on the first pass
thresholds.action: Scale that tier. Keep the winning brand or sales variant.

thresholds.rate: Steady replies, no clear winner yet
thresholds.action: Let it run. Do not mix non-energy TAM into this waterfall.

thresholds.rate: Thin replies after a full first pass
thresholds.action: Swap only the magnet or the first-line hire/launch mention. Do not change the route.

thresholds.rate: No density after a full pass of the tier
thresholds.action: Cut that copy variant. Keep the exclusive waterfall.
